name: MA-06
label: Safe D

key_factors: District's D+11 partisan lean in a heavily Democratic state
Koh's roughly nine-to-one fundraising edge plus $1.8M in outside support versus none for Jones
Prediction markets price the Democratic nominee near 96%
Open seat with no general-election polling adds residual uncertainty
model.rationale: The district's D+11 lean, Dan Koh's roughly nine-to-one fundraising advantage over Micah Jones, and outside spending flowing only to Democrats point to a comfortable Democratic hold of this open seat, and markets price the race near 96% Democratic.
model.watch: Any late general-election polling showing a much tighter race, or a wave of Republican outside spending into the district, would be the first sign the margin is narrowing.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.
Open seat: Seth Moulton (D) is not on the ballot.

overview:
Seth Moulton's retirement to run for Senate leaves this D+11 northeastern Massachusetts district open, and the structural advantages sit firmly with Democrats. Dan Koh has raised $5.4 million to Micah Jones's $620,000, holds a wide cash-on-hand lead, and benefits from about $1.8 million in outside support with no recorded outside spending against him. Prediction markets put Democratic odds near 96%.

No general-election polls or expert ratings are available, so the outlook rests on district fundamentals and the money gap. The seat has been in Democratic hands, and the partisan lean points to a comfortable margin. The open-seat dynamic and absence of polling leave some room for a closer contest than fundamentals suggest, but a Republican win would require a substantial shift.
